messages:
alex: Customer (Acme) sees inconsistent embedding dims from /v1/embeddings when they send batches of 10. Happening ~5% of requests. They said vectors sometimes come back length 1536 and sometimes 0 or 1. Request id: rid_0a9f3c2b.

maya: Do we have the raw payload & headers? also curious if they use gzip or a proxy.

alex: Pasted the exact curl they used (token sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings\" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-1","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3","doc4","doc5","doc6","doc7","doc8","doc9","doc10"]}'
```
Response headers showed 200 but body had fewer vectors than inputs in some cases.

oscar: Can you paste the server-side request_id from our logs? rid_0a9f3c2b is the client id, looking for r-srv...

alex: Server log for that window: 
```
2026-05-12T15:23:11Z svc-embed ingest batch=527 size=10 r-srv=rs_9f3b1 error=\"partial_write\" proto=1.1
2026-05-12T15:23:11Z svc-embed warn  r-srv=rs_9f3b1 client_req=rid_0a9f3c2b returned_vectors=7
2026-05-12T15:23:12Z lb      info  conn=ab12fd status=200 srv_resp=truncated
```
No 401 in this trace, looks like a partial body.

maya: Interesting — partial_write suggests upstream closed the response stream mid-body. Ever seen this with gzip + chunked? Could be client or our LB chopping. Customer on K8s behind an ALB?

alex: They are on Acme infra (AWS ALB) and use a custom HTTP client in Go. They said they set 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' and also use keepalive.

oscar: Two quick asks: 1) can the customer run a curl with --no-buffer and provide --trace-ascii output? 2) can we get a debug bundle from our side (request traces + LB logs) for rs_9f3b1 time window? I'll check KV cache codepath for early return.

ingrid-bot: Debug bundle created: https://internal.redwood/debug-bundles/rs_9f3b1-20260512.tar.gz (access: eng only)

alex: Sent the ask to the customer, asked for the curl variant below and the --trace-ascii output: 
```
curl -v --trace-ascii trace.txt -X POST 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' \
  --data-binary '{"model":"embed-large-1","input":["...10 docs..."]}' \
  --compressed
```
Also asked them to try without --compressed and with a single input to see difference.

maya: Meanwhile, from the internal debug bundle I see repeated log pattern: 
```
serving: start batch id=527 inputs=10
serving: serialize payload -> 10 items
net: write chunk len=2345
net: write chunk len=0 err=EOF
serving: completed 7 vectors, client closed connection
```
Suggests client closed connection or LB reset before we finished streaming JSON.

oscar: If client closed mid-stream we should still return 499 or 502 rather than partial 200 with fewer vectors. I'll open a runtime PR to validate full write or fail the request. For immediate mitigation, ask support to recommend client retries and set smaller batch size.

alex: Customer provided trace.txt. They see the same: server sends a full JSON stream but connection gets RST from ALB after ~1.2s. Trace shows Content-Length absent and Transfer-Encoding: chunked.

maya: ALB default idle/timeouts could be interfering. If their client thinks response done earlier it may close. Also note: some Go HTTP clients incorrectly treat gzipped chunk boundaries. Recommend they set 'Accept-Encoding' off and see if stable.

sre-oncall: Assigning INC-2026-045 to investigate LB timeouts and connection resets 15:23:10-15:23:20 UTC. Pulling vpc flow logs + ALB logs now.

oscar: Action items: (1) engineering will patch runtime to detect partial responses and return 5xx/4xx instead of 200+partial vectors (PR in progress). (2) Support to ask customer to disable compression or reduce batch size to 5 as a workaround. (3) SRE to confirm ALB resets.

alex: I told Acme support engineer to try the two workarounds; they will reply with results. I also attached the customer request id and our server id to ticket.

maya: Thanks — keep thread updated when customer confirms or SRE finds LB reset cause.

oscar: I'll follow up on the runtime PR and link it here when available.

sre-oncall: ALB logs show a 504 between ALB and svc-embed around that time; attaching snippet in the ticket. Looks like backend took longer and ALB closed.

alex: Noted. Keeping the ticket open until customer validates workaround.

maya: tagging this for postmortem if we find a server-side fix needed.

oscar: filed ENG-1058 to hard-fail on partial writes.

alex: thanks all.
